old: Digest. PROVES: Theorem 3.1 (L256): for partial f on S inside G_n, Q_eps(f)/sqrt(1-2 sqrt(eps(1-eps))) >= SA(f)=WA(f)=SWA(f)=MM(f)=SMM(f)=GSA(f)=Theta(KA(f)), the spectral adversary being SA(f)=max_Gamma lambda(Gamma)/max_i lambda(Gamma o D_i) over non-negative symmetric Gamma with Gamma o F=Gamma (L265, formula 3.1). The equalities are Theorem 4.3 and 4.4 (SA=WA=SWA, L468, L514), 5.1 and 5.2, 6.1 and 7.1-7.2 (Kolmogorov, L699); the lower bound on Q is not new: the proof closes by quoting one known bound, for example Ambainis for WA on Boolean f (L733). Theorem 3.2 (L362) gives limits: MM(f) <= 2 sqrt(C_1 n) for partial f and MM(f) <= sqrt(C_0 C_1) for total f (certificate complexities). Derived constant at eps=1/3: 1-2 sqrt(2/9) is about 0.0572, so Q_(1/3) >= about 0.239 SA (arithmetic here, not stated in the paper). QUARTIC USES (lem-A.2 and lem-A.3.lambda in Appendix A): only the lower-bound direction, that the non-negative spectral adversary ratio is a quantum lower bound, as the route to lambda(f)=O(Q(f)) (quartic-ref-03 Lemma 7 cites Barnum-Saks-Szegedy for the same). Adjudication R2-C-BSS had this paper held but not reread; read now, and the statement matches the audit. The original Barnum-Saks-Szegedy paper (ref 7) is not held, so the primary source for Q >= SA stays outside the corpus; the quartic text proves lem-A.2 itself, so no step depends on this paper (adjudication). Licence/metadata caution from the audit: the input file labels this 2004 arXiv submission with an assumed licence; prefer the final publisher copy.
